operatorConstraint: Reflection describes reversal or duality, not forward transport.
question: Does the retained sixteen-face route support an ordinary or a dual-reference four-block return?
macroStep: Four consecutive actual shared-face crossings of a retained route. This is a declared granularity, not a derived native generator.
state: Retain fibre identity, route-program identity, orientation chart, block position, actual cell, payload and accumulated traversal history.
duality: Reflect the entire carrier and route assignment through the fixed reading's middle plane. Preserve fibre identity under the existing paired-presentation convention; retain the chart change.
halfReturnComparator: After four macrosteps, compare the terminal active reference with the reflected initial reference. Do not identify dual references as literal equal states.
secondLeg: Construct a candidate continuation along the reflected whole route, starting at the same exit N body. This adds a dual chart to the route program; report every interface absent from the original forward assignment. Reflection itself is not an executed hop.
testOrder: Validate the carrier reflection and all reflected faces
Compare reflected routes with inverse routes under fixed fibre identities
Validate every physical hop in both legs
Test four-block ordinary and twisted reference return
Test eight-block active reference return with retained history
negativeControls: Reject applying the ordinary Per4 theorem to the retained oriented program
Reject equating return of the active reference with equality of full history-bearing states
Reject counting a dual-only face as used in the original assignment
scope: Conditional geometric corridor executor using the earlier arbitrary-cell-turn and multiplexing policy. Neither the original route selection nor the dual continuation is a source-canonical native operation. No pair-content map or cone filling is supplied.
